promoted_claim: The capital-flow thesis should be proven as a chain from capital source to funding vehicle to company to asset or backlog to operating output to cash return to durability to safe claim.
do_not_say_yet: The full chain has already been proven across all sectors and companies.
strongest_evidence: Big-picture remaining-work map defines the 12 proof layers and current dashboards track status buckets.
missing_evidence: Company-role taxonomy, funding-wrapper classification, asset/project registry, and durability time series are still incomplete.
promotion_test: Promote only after repeated source-to-use-to-output evidence exists across multiple sectors and outside denominators support the scale claim.
disproof_test: Evidence remains anecdotal, single-company, or contradicted by denominators.

promoted_claim: Ares and other alternative managers are large credit-routing platforms with measurable AUM, direct-lending AUM, deployment, and borrower examples.
do_not_say_yet: Private credit is broadly replacing banks across lending markets.
strongest_evidence: Ares Q2 2026 platform rows show 671.319B USD AUM, 440.544B USD Credit Group AUM, 285.725B USD U.S. plus European direct-lending AUM, and 8.2B USD Q2 U.S. direct-lending commitments across 69 transactions.
missing_evidence: Lane-matched bank denominator comparisons and repeated borrower-level bank-facility termination cases.
promotion_test: Promote broader share-take only when private-credit growth is matched to shrinking or displaced bank credit in the same borrower lanes.
disproof_test: Bank credit grows in the same lanes or banks remain agent/revolver/ancillary lenders after private-credit loans close.

promoted_claim: Private credit reaches named borrowers in identifiable industries, and several borrower exposures are visible in SEC-filed holder schedules.
do_not_say_yet: Visible BDC fair value equals total borrower debt or total facility size.
strongest_evidence: Atwell, AeriTek, Frontline, MAI, Precinmac, Relation, Sunvair, and Valcourt crosswalks show borrower-level debt or commitment rows across BDC and private-credit vehicles.
missing_evidence: Full facility sizes, lender groups, use-of-proceeds, and direct mapping from holder rows to transaction facilities.
promotion_test: Promote facility-size claims only when the total facility is disclosed or reconstructed from complete documents.
disproof_test: Partial holder rows are mistaken for total debt or cannot be linked to the relevant transaction.

promoted_claim: Specific borrower-level bank-facility takeout can be proven in selected cases such as Auctane/Stamps.com, while broad bank replacement remains unproven.
do_not_say_yet: Banks are disappearing from corporate lending.
strongest_evidence: Auctane/Stamps.com closing 8-K confirms termination of a prior credit agreement naming Wells Fargo, JPMorgan Chase Bank, and Bank of America; Medallia has repayment evidence.
missing_evidence: Repeated cases across borrower lanes plus post-close bank-role maps and lane-matched bank denominators.
promotion_test: Promote pattern language only after multiple borrower cases show prior bank repayment or termination and new lender-role evidence.
disproof_test: Borrower documents show bank coexistence, agent roles, revolvers, treasury services, or no actual bank-facility repayment.

promoted_claim: Apollo/Athene, KKR/Global Atlantic, Brookfield, and Blackstone show a measurable insurance or retirement-linked credit supply channel.
do_not_say_yet: All insurance assets are private credit or all insurance risk has moved outside banks.
strongest_evidence: Apollo/Athene invested assets and inflows; KKR/Global Atlantic credit AUM and insurance investments; Brookfield allocation rows; Blackstone insurance SMA inflows.
missing_evidence: Statutory Schedule D/BA, NAIC designations, capital and surplus, rating reports, impairments, affiliated investment detail, and borrower destination links.
promotion_test: Promote quality and borrower-destination claims only when liability scale, asset allocation, and credit quality are quantified in the same period.
disproof_test: Statutory data shows mostly public investment-grade exposure, weak capital, impairments, or immaterial private-credit allocation.

promoted_claim: Some large-load and power-demand evidence has moved into tariffs, ESAs, dockets, and utility planning processes.
do_not_say_yet: AI demand has already created fully funded in-service power assets everywhere.
strongest_evidence: AEP Ohio and Duke materials include tariff, LOA, ESA, collateral, minimum-demand, exit-fee, generation procurement, and docket evidence.
missing_evidence: Operating-company project status, MW, dollar capex, customer identity where allowed, recovery mechanism, approval status, and in-service timing.
promotion_test: Promote project-grade load claims only when demand is tied to approved project dollars, MW, contracts, and recovery mechanism.
disproof_test: Load pipeline is cancelled, speculative, not approved, or not tied to recoverable project spend.

promoted_claim: Utilities can fund approved assets with debt/equity and recover costs from customers when regulators authorize rate-base or rider treatment.
do_not_say_yet: Every utility capex dollar is recoverable at attractive returns.
strongest_evidence: Utility denominator maps and dockets show rate-base, capex, rider, and approval entry points for selected companies and jurisdictions.
missing_evidence: Rate-case orders, allowed ROE, capital structure, rider mechanics, regulatory lag, disallowances, and customer bill impacts.
promotion_test: Promote recoverable-capital claims only by jurisdiction and docket after approval or clear rider mechanism exists.
disproof_test: Regulators deny recovery, lower allowed ROE, impose disallowances, or delay cost recovery.

promoted_claim: ET and Cheniere show capital flowing into identifiable energy infrastructure, LNG cargo conversion, export capacity, debt stacks, contracted production, and bounded physical-output evidence; Cheniere has the strongest partial entity/cargo bridge.
do_not_say_yet: Project-level source-of-funds, returns, and customer economics are fully proven for every named asset.
strongest_evidence: ET/Cheniere source-table, annual baseline, DOE LNG cargo, EIA export denominator, credit/debt extraction rows, and energy project source-use-return pass.
missing_evidence: Named-project cost, financing source, use allocation, FERC/train status, customer contract economics, entity waterfall, debt service, and return evidence.
promotion_test: Promote project-and-cash-grade claims only when project cost, funding, physical output, customer economics, debt service, and waterfall controls are joined.
disproof_test: Capex is maintenance, project delayed, customer economics weak, output cannot be attributed, or funding cannot be tied to the named project.

promoted_claim: United Rentals is a fleet-access capital absorber with visible fleet OEC, rental capex, operating cash flow, used-equipment proceeds, and collateralized funding stack.
do_not_say_yet: All URI fleet capex is high-return growth capex or fully collateral-protected funding.
strongest_evidence: URI annual/Q2 source rows show OEC, rental capex, operating cash flow, fleet productivity, liquidity, ABL, AR securitization, and debt stack evidence.
missing_evidence: Borrowing-base detail, advance rates, eligible collateral, fleet utilization, fleet mix, maintenance/growth split, and loss/liquidation assumptions.
promotion_test: Promote collateral-grade claims only after borrowing-base and fleet-collateral details are extracted.
disproof_test: Fleet productivity weakens, utilization falls, collateral eligibility is lower than assumed, or capex is mostly replacement.

promoted_claim: Sterling is a conversion-supported customer-project execution and acquisition platform whose funding need is timing, retainage, bonding/L/C support, working capital, capex, acquisitions, and backlog conversion.
do_not_say_yet: Sterling's entire backlog is fully customer-funded, non-cancellable, organic, high-margin, and risk-free.
strongest_evidence: Sterling agreement-term, customer-funding, covenant-cushion, eight-quarter conversion, acquired-versus-organic, L/C/surety, and backlog credit-platform conversion passes show 1.500B USD revolver, 600M USD L/C sublimit, 646.306M USD Q2 2026 net contract-liability timing, RPO growth from 2.055081B USD to 4.233618B USD, positive quarterly OCF less capex across the eight-quarter table, and 2.56B USD of CEC/Stone Ridge acquired signed and unsigned backlog visibility.
missing_evidence: Actual post-reset L/C usage, bonded backlog, formal covenant calculations, project-owner source-of-funds, margin by project, cancellation economics, and source-to-project credit allocation.
promotion_test: Promote project-source-grade claims only when customer funding, L/C/surety usage, backlog conversion, project margin, and cash data are visible by project or segment.
disproof_test: Backlog fails to convert, unsigned awards do not become contracts, working-capital reverses, or acquired backlog is low-margin.

promoted_claim: Funding type appears to follow asset type: networks, contracted LNG entities, reusable collateral, backlog platforms, and regulated assets use different funding wrappers.
do_not_say_yet: Funding reason is proven for every company or every project.
strongest_evidence: Funding-type hypothesis map, filed-credit term summary, agreement extraction, URI/Cheniere/ET/Sterling evidence, and Sterling wrapper/cushion passes.
missing_evidence: More companies classified by wrapper; covenant/collateral/waterfall/recovery proof; disproof tests by funding type.
promotion_test: Promote theory as pattern-proven only after multiple examples per wrapper have source-backed collateral/cash-flow/recovery logic.
disproof_test: Funding wrappers do not line up with collateral quality, legal separability, contracted cash flows, or recovery mechanisms.

promoted_claim: Some lanes show real output conversion: Cheniere cargoes match DOE vessel rows, URI is a repeated-period fleet capital-to-output proxy case, and Sterling is a conversion-supported backlog/acquisition execution platform.
do_not_say_yet: Every capex, backlog, revolver, L/C capacity, or AUM number represents productive real-economy investment.
strongest_evidence: DOE LNG cargo match, URI operating conversion scorecard, Sterling backlog credit-platform conversion pass, utility docket/project rows, and Ares borrower follow-through examples.
missing_evidence: ET/LNG project-level source-of-funds, grid/power conversion scorecards, project/segment margin, utilization, cash, and external denominators.
promotion_test: Promote operating-output claims only when dollars connect to physical output or revenue/cash conversion with period, source, and boundary controls.
disproof_test: Capex is maintenance, backlog is unfunded, utilization weakens, cash conversion reverses, or output cannot be tied to funding.

promoted_claim: Outside denominators are necessary before turning company evidence into market claims.
do_not_say_yet: A few company examples prove a market-wide capital shift.
strongest_evidence: FRED bank denominators; EIA/DOE LNG/NGL denominators; Census construction and data-center denominators; project denominator workbench.
missing_evidence: Consistent denominator map by lane: bank credit, private credit, utility load, construction, fleet rental, LNG exports, public funding, and insurer asset allocation.
promotion_test: Promote market-scale claims only when company evidence is compared with relevant outside denominator trends.
disproof_test: External datasets show the opposite trend or company examples are immaterial relative to market size.

promoted_claim: Many current findings are strong snapshots, but URI and Sterling now have repeated-period operating-conversion evidence at proxy grade.
do_not_say_yet: A single quarter proves a durable capital-flow thesis.
strongest_evidence: Annual/Q2 baselines exist for several lanes; URI has a 12-row operating conversion scorecard; Sterling has eight-quarter contract-capital conversion plus acquired-versus-organic and L/C/surety boundary passes; private-credit and insurance platform metrics have repeated-period starts.
missing_evidence: Eight-quarter or multi-year time series for ET/LNG, grid/power, private-credit borrower use, source stacks, bank-role outcomes, and remaining operating lanes.
promotion_test: Promote trend-proven claims only after repeated metrics show consistent direction and conversion with source, period, and boundary controls.
disproof_test: The time series shows reversal, one-time acquisition effects, weak utilization, cash-flow timing reversal, or missing source-to-output linkage.

promoted_claim: The 519-company universe now has a role/wrapper/proof extraction template that routes every company into a lane, expected funding wrapper, source-availability status, proof level, denominator need, next-document target, safe claim, and do-not-claim boundary.
do_not_say_yet: The 519-company universe is source-proven or representative of the final thesis.
strongest_evidence: 519-company triage, lane candidate queues, all-company scale-up model, all-company extraction template, theme evidence program, and big-picture remaining-work map.
missing_evidence: Lane-specific primary-source extraction, evidence upgrades, denominator checks, and claim refreshes from the template.
promotion_test: Promote all-company empirical coverage only after template rows are upgraded by lane-specific source extraction.
disproof_test: Template rows remain radar-only, high-signal backlog, monitor, or selected queue status without source extraction.
